transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in today?

I've been feeling incredibly down and I've completely lost interest in all my usual hobbies. It's been going on for about eight months now, and I just don't have the motivation to do anything anymore.
Have you felt depressed or lost interest most days for at least two years, or has this been a more recent episode lasting less than two years?
It hasn't been as long as two years. This is a more recent episode, and it has been going on for about eight months now.
Have you been having trouble sleeping, sleeping too much, or waking up much earlier than usual?
I haven't really noticed any major changes with my sleep. I seem to sleep normally, so that hasn't been an issue for me.
Have you noticed any change in your appetite or weight recently, either eating much less or much more than usual?

Yes, my appetite has been almost nonexistent nearly every day lately. I've lost a lot of weight because of it, probably more than five percent of my body weight in just the last month, without even trying to diet.
Have you been feeling very guilty or worthless, or blaming yourself excessively for things lately?
No, I haven't really been feeling guilty or blaming myself for things. I just feel very empty and flat, but I don't feel like I've done anything wrong.
Have you had any thoughts that you would be better off dead, or thoughts of hurting yourself?
No, I haven't had any thoughts of hurting myself or wishing I were dead. Even though I feel very empty, those kinds of thoughts haven't crossed my mind.

Based on the interview so far, this pattern is most consistent with Major Depressive Disorder. One important next question would be whether you've ever had periods of unusually high energy, decreased need for sleep, or feeling abnormally euphoric or irritable, which would suggest bipolar disorder instead.
No, I have never experienced anything like that. I've never had those kinds of high-energy periods or felt abnormally happy and active. My energy has always been on the lower side, especially lately.
Thank you. Based on everything you've told me, your symptoms are most consistent with Major Depressive Disorder.

That makes sense, but how do the strange things I've been hearing and the terrifying thoughts I've had fit into depression? These scary experiences only ever seem to happen when I am feeling deeply depressed. Can depression actually cause things like that?
